market.headline: Tech is under pressure ahead of Nvidia's earnings on Tuesday night.
points: Chips: Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close, its first results since CEO Jensen Huang left. That one report can move every tech stock on Wednesday.
Politics: After the Nov 3 midterms, traders worry about tighter AI and data centre rules. A Trump-Xi summit this week adds trade headlines.
Rates: October inflation came in hot and the 10-year US bond yield is above 5%. Higher rates usually weigh on pricey growth stocks.
Events: The Anthropic IPO later this week will test how much appetite is left for AI names.
market.plan: Go slow this week. Buy steady names in small pieces now, and leave chip names until Wednesday when Nvidia's numbers are out.

stocks.sum: The simple, certified way to own about 210 halal US companies at once.
why: Down about 7% from its high, so you are not buying at the top.
One purchase spreads your money over many companies, so one bad stock hurts less.
Certified halal, so there is no screening homework.
risk: About 44% of it sits in five big tech names, so it still falls when tech falls.
stocks.todo: Good first purchase. Buy half now and half after Nvidia reports.

stocks.sum: A calm, Canadian-dollar halal fund. No currency fee when you buy it.
why: Trades in Canadian dollars, so you skip the 1.5% US currency fee each way.
Holds about 150 steady companies around the world and moves much less than tech.
Certified halal.
risk: Slow mover. Good for safety, weak for quick gains.
My price here is old. Check today's price in Wealthsimple.
stocks.todo: A sensible place for money you can't afford to see swing, like a down payment.

stocks.n: SP Funds Dow Jones Global Sukuk ETF
stocks.sum: A halal income fund that pays monthly, about 4.9% a year. Not a growth play.
why: Pays a small amount every month.
Barely moves when stocks drop.
risk: The price sits near its 52-week low and has gone nowhere for five years.
US withholding tax takes 15% of the payouts inside an FHSA.
stocks.todo: Only use it to park cash for income. It will not help a few-month profit goal.

stocks.earnNote: Nvidia, its biggest driver, reports Nov 17
stocks.sum: The chip rebound trade without leverage, spread over 25 chip makers.
why: About 28% below its high, so there is real room to recover.
Chip stocks are priced at their cheapest in years compared with their profits.
risk: It moves almost twice as much as the market. It fell 11% in one day on Nov 5.
Nvidia's results on Tuesday night will swing it hard either way.
stocks.todo: Wait for Nvidia's results. If chips hold up on Wednesday, buy one share.

stocks.sum: The AI chip leader, down a third and in the middle of a leadership crisis.
why: About 33% below its high, and cheap against its expected profits.
Analysts' average target is far above today's price.
risk: Earnings land Tuesday night, the first since the CEO left. A 10% move overnight is normal for this stock.
Eleven analysts cut their rating last week, and there is talk of tighter export rules.
stocks.todo: Do not buy before earnings. Look again Wednesday morning.

stocks.sum: A big winner from custom AI chips, about 30% below its high.
why: Money leaving Nvidia has been flowing into Broadcom.
Analysts' average target is roughly 50% above the price.
risk: It was downgraded on Friday and fell nearly 7% that day.
Earnings on Dec 9 are the next big test.
stocks.todo: Wait until after Nvidia reports. If you buy, plan to be out or smaller before Dec 9.

stocks.sum: Strong business, but the wildest stock on this list.
why: Record quarter on Nov 3 and gaining ground on Nvidia.
risk: It fell about 9% on Friday alone and moves two and a half times as much as the market.
Very expensive against current profits, so bad news hits it hard.
stocks.todo: Skip it for now. A normal stop can't protect you well on a stock that swings this much.

stocks.sum: Makes the chips for nearly every AI company, so it wins whoever leads.
why: About 18% below its high with a reasonable price against profits.
Less tied to the Nvidia leadership story than other chip names.
risk: It still dropped 10.8% in the Nov 5 chip selloff.
Taiwan and US-China politics are a standing risk, and a Trump-Xi summit is on this week.
stocks.todo: Wait for Nvidia's results and the summit headlines, then consider one share.

stocks.sum: The steady one. It held up through the whole chip selloff.
why: Only about 6% below its high while chip stocks fell 30%, which shows buyers trust it.
Moves about the same as the market, so the stop can be tighter.
Earnings are already out, so no surprise is due soon.
risk: One share is about $745 CAD, a big piece of a small account.
It had a service outage last week. It is fixed, but watch for follow-up news.
stocks.todo: A fair buy for one share. A limit order a little under today's price is fine.

stocks.sum: The cheapest big tech name against its profits, about 28% below its high.
why: Its price-to-earnings is near 15, the lowest of the seven biggest tech companies.
Its income comes from ads and cloud, so it depends less on chip spending.
Earnings are already out.
risk: It trades close to its 52-week low. Cheap stocks can get cheaper.
A class action was filed this month and ad revenue has been soft.
stocks.todo: Buy one share now and a second after Nvidia reports.

stocks.sum: A safe haven lately, but priced at the top.
why: Investors moved into Apple while chips fell.
risk: It sits about 1% below its all-time high and already above analysts' average target.
Pricey against profits, so there is little room left for a few-month trade.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Put it on your list for a pullback of 8% or more.

stocks.sum: A story stock. The price runs on headlines more than on profits.
why: About 22% below its high, and Cybercab pre-orders have opened.
risk: Extremely expensive against its profits.
It is reported to be winding down Cybertruck production, and it swings on every headline.
stocks.todo: Skip for a planned, rule-based trade. Too unpredictable.

stocks.sum: Reasonably priced and 18% below its high, but the halal status needs your own check.
why: Fair price against profits, and analysts' target is well above today's price.
risk: Halal screeners do not all agree on Meta. Check Zoya or Musaffa first.
Italy fined it about $887 million this month, and it is spending heavily on AI.
stocks.todo: Settle the halal question first. If it passes for you, treat it like Alphabet.

stocks.sum: The weight-loss drug leader, sitting at a record high.
why: Not a tech stock, so it spreads your risk.
It barely moves with the market.
risk: At its high and right at analysts' average target, so the easy gains are behind it.
One share costs about $2,050 CAD.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Too big for one share on a $10,000 account, and no discount.

stocks.sum: A defensive stock that investors ran to during the tech selloff.
why: Very calm. It hardly reacts to market drops.
risk: At its high and above analysts' average target, so you would be buying after the run.
Ongoing talc lawsuits.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Good company, wrong price for a new trade.
